title.narrative: Inter-agency translation and interpretation services to strengthen humanitarian response coordination in Myanmar

description.narrative:
ltpgtlt/pgtltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-top:9.95pt"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtLocal organizations are at the heart of the humanitarian response in Myanmar, providing immediate assistance to people in need using their local knowledge, skills, networks, and comparatively wider access. Language has been identified as a critical participation barrier for local organizations, and thus simultaneous interpretation in meetings and translation of critical documents from English to Myanmar languages (Burmese and other locally relevant languages) and vice versa are crucial to ensure the inclusion of local actors in coordination structures and enable them to receive clear, timely and actionable information for effective humanitarian response to affected people. IOM, in close coordination with the OCHA Coordination Support section, has developed a language service team (the Translation Interpretation Team (TI here forth) to improve information sharing between the various coordination mechanisms and local actors in the right language and format via relevant channels (translation of critical documents, simultaneous interpretation in meetings) at the national level.lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom:9.95pt"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtltbrgt The objective of this intervention is to strengthen the localization of the response through active coordination between national actors and international humanitarian partners, including UN agencies and INGOs. IOM has hired hire a team of interpreters and translators working full time with cluster coordinators and other key stakeholders at the national level to strengthen humanitarian response coordination in Myanmar. Translators are providing on an ongoing basis simultaneous interpretation and translation services. The interpretation services are used during monthly national level coordination meetings (including cluster and working group meetings) to encourage representatives from local NGOs (LNGOs) and Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) to provide inputs and actively participate to the discussions. Some clusters have also started using the service at sub-national level. The written translation services are provided in coordination with national level cluster coordinators and OCHA to improve the access to information of local actors, which greatly benefits national partners to openly advocate for the needs of vulnerable communities in line with humanitarian principles and the Grand Bargain commitments. The initial pilot of this project ran from 1 October 2022 to 30 June 2023, and underwent a 2 month no cost extension until 31 August 2023. Due to the success of the first phase of the project, further funds to cover the project from 1 September to 29 February is urgently requested to maintain the services beyond 31 August 2023.lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtIn addition to this, OCHA requested that IOM further extend its support to the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group through the procurement of a one-year license of the software programme ActivityInfo, which is a vital tool to monitor the humanitarian response in Myanmar. The ICCG at its meeting on 3 May 2023 endorsed the recommendation of the IM Working Group to use ActivityInfo across the entire humanitarian operation and called upon OCHA to seek funding through MHF. Joining these support functions in one project is the most efficient way for IOM to support the wider coordination. lt/spangtlt/pgt
